prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Choose Your Companion Deck", "Species & Trait Selector"]
1: ["Preview Your Desktop Pet Landing", "See how your pet sits on your taskbar and interacts with open desktop windows."]
2: ["Verify & Connect Your Pet Cloud Account", "Scans and verifies cloud pet retention before confirming login.", "Cloud Save Verification Status"]
3: ["Select Your Desktop Companion Pathway"]
4: ["Signing into an existing account will automatically sync and protect your previous pet data."]
5: ["Taskbar & Visibility Tips"]
6: ["Official Adoption Certificate & Starter Gift", "Bonus Starter Accessory Included"]
7: ["Play Chime When Companion Arrives"]
8: ["Your Companion is Live on Your Desktop!", "Right-click your pet anytime or click the system tray icon to access controls, talk, or hide your companion."]
9: ["Photo Quality Diagnostic", "Checking lighting and pet face visibility for perfect rendering...", "Analyzing image clarity"]

verdicts.problem: Mentions gifts and free extra items
